Back-transform posterior draws to the original trait scale

Source: R/size_shape.R
back_transform.Rd

Takes a fit of the size and shape scores made with lmm_animal and returns draws of the genetic and residual covariance matrices, the phenotypic covariance, the genetic correlations and the heritabilities on the scale of the original traits.

Usage

back_transform(fit, transform)

Arguments

fit

A fit returned by lmm_animal (a CmdStanMCMC object), or a posterior draws object, or a matrix of draws, containing the variables G and E, or P for a phenotypic fit from lm_phen_cov.

transform

A size_shape object from size_shape.

Value

A list of class size_shape_draws holding one element per quantity, in the same layout as lmm_animal_gibbs: traits first and draws last, with every dimension named after the traits. For an animal fit it holds G, E, P, corrG and corrP as traits by traits by draws arrays, and h2 as a traits by draws matrix. For a phenotypic fit it holds P and corrP as arrays and sigma_P as a matrix. traits holds the trait names.

Details

For each draw the covariance matrices are mapped as \(M \to B M B^T\), which is exact because size and shape are a linear reparametrization of the traits. Heritabilities and correlations are then recomputed from the transformed matrices: unlike the covariance, they are not invariant under a change of traits, so the h2 of a shape axis is not the h2 of any original trait.

The fixed effects beta stay on the model scale, since a coefficient for size or a shape axis does not correspond to a single original trait.

Draws are the last dimension, as in lmm_animal_gibbs, so posterior summaries are direct: draws_mean(post, "G") is the posterior mean of G on the trait scale, and draws_quantile(post, "corrG", probs = 0.05) its 5% quantile. fit_draws also accepts this object and returns the same arrays.

See also

size_shape, rename_beta, to_draws_list

Examples

ss <- size_shape(cbind(a = rnorm(20), b = rnorm(20), c = rnorm(20)))
k <- length(ss$raw_traits)
names_mat <- function(var) sprintf(paste0(var, "[%d,%d]"),
                                   rep(seq_len(k), k), rep(seq_len(k), each = k))
# a real fit supplies G and E; here the same draw is repeated
G <- random_covariance(k, min_var = 0.5, max_var = 1.5)
E <- random_covariance(k, min_var = 0.5, max_var = 1.5)
m <- cbind(matrix(rep(as.vector(G), 4), 4, byrow = TRUE),
           matrix(rep(as.vector(E), 4), 4, byrow = TRUE))
colnames(m) <- c(names_mat("G"), names_mat("E"))
post <- back_transform(m, ss)
dim(post$G)                    # traits x traits x draws
#> [1] 3 3 4
draws_mean(post, "G")          # posterior mean G on the trait scale
#>           a         b         c
#> a 2.4148785 0.5599549 0.2250826
#> b 0.5599549 0.8963117 0.2172248
#> c 0.2250826 0.2172248 1.0309030
draws_mean(post, "h2")
#>         a         b         c 
#> 0.4483425 0.5086840 0.3443663
